children: RBI’s decision to reject Tata Sons’ request to give up its NBFC registration brings the group’s long-delayed listing back into focus

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has rejected Tata Sons’ request to surrender its registration as a Core Investment Company (CIC), leaving the Tata Group holding company under the central bank’s non-banking financial company (NBFC) framework.

The decision is significant because Tata Sons had sought to exit the NBFC framework, which would have helped it avoid the mandatory listing requirement for companies classified under the RBI’s Upper Layer category.

Tata Sons had applied to surrender its CIC registration in March 2024 after repaying more than Rs 21,000 crore of debt. The company had argued that it no longer needed to remain registered as an NBFC after becoming debt-free.
RBI Decision Keeps Listing Issue Alive
Tata Sons was classified as an Upper Layer NBFC by the RBI in 2022. Companies in this category are required to list their shares within the prescribed timeline.
Tata Sons did not proceed with a public listing while its application to surrender the licence was being considered. The RBI’s latest decision now leaves the company facing the listing requirement.

The issue has been closely watched because Tata Sons is the holding company for several major Tata Group businesses. Its portfolio includes stakes in companies such as Tata Consultancy Services, Tata Motors and Tata Consumer Products.
The RBI’s decision also comes after changes to the regulatory framework for Upper Layer NBFCs. Tata Sons remains within the category under the revised rules, keeping the listing question relevant.
Tata Sons IPO Timeline Remains Unclear
The RBI’s decision does not mean Tata Sons has announced an initial public offering (IPO). The company has not disclosed when or how it could proceed with a listing.
A public listing would also bring greater disclosure requirements and allow investors to value Tata Sons and its investments through the market.

The issue has divided shareholders. Tata Trusts, the largest shareholder in Tata Sons, has been opposed to a listing, while the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which owns a significant stake, has supported the idea.
The focus will now shift to how Tata Sons responds to the RBI’s decision and what steps it takes to meet the regulatory requirements.
